LESSON: READING 4.2.1 INTENSIVE READING

Grade: Grade 9
Subject: ENGLISH
Strand: Strand 4
Topic 4.2: Reading 4.2.1 Intensive Reading

SECTION 1: WELCOME

Hello! This is a study lesson on Reading 4.2.1 Intensive Reading. Read the explanation, follow every worked example, then do the practice. This is original CBC Learn content written from KICD outcomes — not a copy of a commercial textbook.

Big question: How are characters and events in a text related to real life?

SECTION 2: WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

By the end of this lesson, you will be able to:

1. answer direct and inferential questions for comprehension
2. appreciate the importance of intensive reading in lifelong learning

SECTION 3: STUDY NOTES (READ AND LEARN)

WHAT YOU ARE STUDYING: READING 4.2.1 INTENSIVE READING
Subject: ENGLISH · Grade: Grade 9
This is a learner study lesson (not a teacher guide). Read every part, follow the models, then practise.

BIG PICTURE
Reading 4.2.1 Intensive Reading helps you succeed in ENGLISH. You will understand it, practise it, and use it at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

KEY FACTS: READING 4.2.1 INTENSIVE READING
Language skills grow by daily practice: listen carefully, speak clearly, read every day, write neatly.
Model → guided practice → independent practice.
Always use complete sentences when writing answers.

PART 1: Answer direct and inferential questions for comprehension

What this means
In this part you learn to answer direct and inferential questions for comprehension. You will use ideas from at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: answer direct and inferential questions for comprehension.
2. Listen, speak, read, then write using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Model reading: Read a short paragraph about “Reading 4.2.1 Intensive Reading”, then retell it in 3 sentences.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can answer direct and inferential questions for comprehension. Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 2: Appreciate the importance of intensive reading in lifelong learning

What this means
In this part you learn to appreciate the importance of intensive reading in lifelong learning. You will use ideas from at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: appreciate the importance of intensive reading in lifelong learning.
2. Listen, speak, read, then write using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Model speaking: Say 4 clear sentences about Reading 4.2.1 Intensive Reading to a partner.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can appreciate the importance of intensive reading in lifelong learning. Write or say your answer clearly.

PUT IT TOGETHER
Close your notes and say aloud: what Reading 4.2.1 Intensive Reading is, one example, and one way you will practise this week.

SECTION 4: QUICK EXAMPLES

Example 1: Read a short paragraph about “Reading 4.2.1 Intensive Reading”, then retell it in 3 sentences. (skill: answer direct and inferential questions for comprehension)

Example 2: Say 4 clear sentences about Reading 4.2.1 Intensive Reading to a partner. (skill: appreciate the importance of intensive reading in lifelong learning)

SECTION 5: PRACTICE NOW

1. Write 5 sentences (or show 5 clear steps) that teach Reading 4.2.1 Intensive Reading to a classmate.
2. Practise this skill: answer direct and inferential questions for comprehension.
3. Practise this skill: appreciate the importance of intensive reading in lifelong learning.
4. Make one local Kenya example of Reading 4.2.1 Intensive Reading from your county, market, farm, or school.
5. Mark your own work: What did you get right? What will you redo?

SECTION 6: WORK TO DO (HOME / REVISION)

1. In your exercise book, make a one-page revision sheet for Reading 4.2.1 Intensive Reading: meaning, 3 examples, 5 practice items.
2. Teach a parent/guardian or younger sibling one part of this lesson (2 minutes).
3. Answer in writing: Why should a Grade 9 learner study Reading 4.2.1 Intensive Reading?
4. Prepare for the quiz: cover the Remember box and recite it.

SECTION: THINK ABOUT IT

1. How are characters and events in a text related to real life?
2. Why is note taking an important reading skill?

SECTION: REMEMBER

1. Know what Reading 4.2.1 Intensive Reading means in your own words.
2. Use local Kenyan examples, not only definitions.
3. Practise in small steps, then check your work.
4. Be able to: answer direct and inferential questions for comprehension.
5. Be able to: appreciate the importance of intensive reading in lifelong learning.

Now complete the Revision Quiz. Open Answers only after you finish.

— CBC Learn · Original study notes from KICD outcomes (Strategy 2)
